Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — Memory Transfer Learning (MTL, 'Ours'): a unified cross-domain memory pool retrieved into the coding agent's prompt, compared across four memory formats, against zero-shot and against two self-evolving methods (ReasoningBank, AgentKB) on 6 coding benchmarks (RQ1-RQ3)
fields.why: Format corrected to ' — '. r0 had 'Evaluates; secondary: proposes an approach'. The paper frames itself as an investigation, but introduces MTL as its own method ('We introduce Memory Transfer Learning', 'MTL (Ours)') and compares it with ReasoningBank and AgentKB, which fits the 2026-11-23 rule for studies that propose an approach (Q13 already scored). Author to decide.

fields.v: Memory Transfer Learning (MTL): a unified memory pool from heterogeneous coding benchmarks, retrieved into the agent system prompt; four memory formats: Trajectory, Workflow, Summary, Insight (after ReasoningBank). Compared with ReasoningBank and AgentKB. No version

Memory items generated by an LLM from past agent trajectories: Trajectory (commands and observations), Workflow (goal + key actions), Summary (task summary + experience paragraph), Insight (title, one-sentence description, task-agnostic content). Top-3 memories (cosine similarity on text-embedding-3-small) inserted in the system prompt. No specification document

Offline: run agent on all benchmarks, LLM judge labels success/failure, generate memories with success/failure prompts, build pool excluding the test benchmark, embed. Online: for each task (for non-trajectory formats the model first writes a 4-5 sentence plan as query) retrieve N=3 memories, add to system prompt, agent solves task

fields.why: r0 gave the three zero-shot baselines no verdict ('Baseline.') and judged MTL variants by their change against zero-shot (e.g. 'negative on TB2', '+3.7'); §6 requires each configuration, baseline included, to be judged on its own. On their own, all configurations reach about 0.48-0.57 average Pass@3 with weak results on TB2/RepliB, so quality is partly; cost is not measured. Verdict levels remain a judgement; Table 1 values re-checked and unchanged.

fields.v: Tasks: 6 benchmarks, up to 100 random tasks each. Configurations: zero-shot vs MTL with 4 memory formats (GPT-5-mini) and Insight for DeepSeek V3.2 and Qwen3-Coder-480B; vs ReasoningBank and AgentKB on 3 benchmarks; ablations on abstraction, pool size, domains, cross-model, retrieval. Baseline: zero-shot (no memory). Held constant: agent mini-swe-agent, model within comparison, N=3 memories, harbor evaluation, same LLM for memory generation/judge. Acceptance tests: benchmark evaluation protocols. Repetitions: three runs (Pass@3). Human intervention: none

MTL Insight best format: avg +3.7 points over zero-shot with GPT-5-mini (0.523 to 0.560), up to +8.3 on MLGym; +2.6 DeepSeek, +1.8 Qwen. Ranking Insight > Summary > Workflow > Trajectory; Trajectory hurts TB2 and MLGym. MTL beats ReasoningBank (+2.9) and AgentKB (+1.7) with 431 memories. Simple embedding retrieval beats reranking and rewriting. No significance tests

Distinguished formats and methods on average, with small differences (often 1 task in 100); some benchmarks show no or negative difference. Repeatability: three runs, Pass@3, no variance reported. Limitations of the method: none stated explicitly

No limitations section. Negative transfer (domain-mismatched anchoring, false validation confidence, misapplied best practices); need for better agentic memory retrieval and adaptation (domain routing, step-wise retrieval); cross-model transfer below self-generated memories; impact statement notes risk of unsafe code from misapplied patterns
